finding: `tasks renew` hard-fails with ATM_TASK_CLAIM_OWNER_MISMATCH ('claimed by X, not X') when the lane-session document has expired (30-minute lane-session TTL) even though the claim actor is unchanged and still the lifecycle owner. The renew path enforces a strict lane-id equality check, but each fresh CLI invocation mints a new lane session when the prior lane-session document has passed its 30-minute expiry, so the requested lane never matches the holding lane. Renewing a long-running claim is therefore impossible without falling back to `tasks claim` (idempotent same-actor reentry) to rebind a fresh lane.
expectedBehavior: renew (and other strict-lane actions) should treat an expired-but-same-actor lane session as renewable: mint/rebind a lane session for the resolved owner and continue, or reconcile against claim.actorId when the lane-session document has merely expired. Owner-preserving renew must not require a claim reentry just because the 30-minute lane TTL elapsed.
evidenceOrRepro: The reproduction was confirmed from the current source: an expired referenced lane is resolved to a newly minted lane, then strict lane-id ownership rejects the same actor. Repaired renew to accept only same-actor expired-lane rebinding and persist the new lane metadata on the renewed claim; release and handoff remain strict. Regression `tests/cli/claim-renew-expired-lane.test.ts` proves renew succeeds with a new same-actor lane and release still returns `ATM_LANE_SESSION_OWNERSHIP_MISMATCH`. Also passed `tests/cli/claim-owner-mismatch-message.test.ts`, `npm run typecheck`, `git diff --check`, and encoding guard.
